title: Carbon Management & Net Zero
welcome_lead: Compare mitigation: NbS, CCS and policy.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on carbon mitigation, net zero and nature-based solutions.
final_note: Net zero needs both technology and nature.

concepts.def: Balancing emissions and removals; UK target by 2050.
Pay another party to reduce/absorb emissions on your behalf.
Carbon Capture and Storage; capture flue gas, inject underground.
Bioenergy with CCS; burn biomass, capture CO2; potentially negative emissions.
Forests, wetlands, soil carbon; cost-effective at scale.
2015 UN treaty; limit warming to well below 2 degrees C, aim for 1.5.

walkthroughs.body_html: Paris Agreement (2015) signed by 196 parties. Each submits Nationally Determined Contributions. UNEP Gap Report (2023): current NDCs put world on 2.5-2.9 degrees C path; need 43 percent cut by 2030 vs 2019 levels for 1.5 degrees C. COP28 (Dubai 2023) agreed transition away from fossil fuels.

Boundary Dam (Canada 2014) captures 1 Mt CO2/yr from coal plant. Climeworks Orca (Iceland 2021) direct air capture 4000 t/yr. BECCS modelled as essential for 1.5 degrees C scenarios but unproven at scale. Solar PV cost fell 90 percent 2010-2020.

Reforestation can sequester ~10 Gt C globally if 350 Mha restored (Bonn Challenge). Mangrove and saltmarsh restoration stores blue carbon. UK peatland restoration target: 280000 ha by 2050. Co-benefits include biodiversity, flood risk reduction.
